title: Build the rule in
statement: Where a rule can be built into what a model is given, build it in rather than rely on a check to catch the breach.
detail: In a reading course, a moment that runs before the story replied to a child with the story's plot, though the child hadn't opened it (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-3/CONTENT-FAILURE-CLASSES.md`). The fix that mattered was on the request, not the wording: moments before the passage send the scorer an empty passage and an empty word list, so it cannot quote what the child hasn't read, and a gate with 11 assertions checks it. The course's own lesson from it: a rule you can't violate beats a rule you must remember.

evidence.quote: so it *cannot* quote what the child hasn't read. A rule you can't violate beats a rule you must remember.
